_meta.description: Efficiency, lifetime, temperature range, maintenance, and suitability parameters for decarbonization technologies.
_meta.critical_caveat: IEA figures (Step 8) are global, not India-specific -- use as upper-bound sanity checks and adjust downward using BEE/TERI India-specific figures wherever they conflict. Residential/building-scale heat pump lifetime figures should not be used directly for industrial equipment.

coal_biomass_fired.note: Use as realistic current baseline for coal/biomass boilers in Indian MSMEs (not the optimistic 88-98% figure, which applies mainly to gas/oil).

field_audited_actual_india.note: Commonly below design spec due to excess air, scaling, unburned fuel, radiation losses.

electric_boiler.opex_note: Energy costs considerably higher than gas boiler unless electricity is cheap/subsidized -- capex parity does not mean opex parity.

efficiency_improvement_levers.flue_gas_temp_reduction: every 22C reduction in flue gas exit temperature improves efficiency by ~1%
efficiency_improvement_levers.excess_air_reduction: every 5% reduction in excess air (or 1% reduction in residual stack O2) improves efficiency by ~1%

boiler.common_type_india: fire-tube (Scotch marine) boilers most common in small-to-medium Indian factories; water-tube boilers used in larger/higher-pressure applications

lifetime_years.lifetime_caveat: IEA's 17-year figure is for residential/building-scale gas boilers -- use the project's own 15-year industrial assumption as primary.

furnace.efficiency_benchmark: No single clean benchmark exists (unlike boilers) -- BEE calculates efficiency indirectly by subtracting known losses (flue gas sensible heat, moisture loss, opening losses, wall/structure losses) from 100%. Highly process- and temperature-specific.
furnace.modeling_recommendation: Model furnace efficiency as a function of operating temperature and fuel type rather than a flat percentage.

motor.standard_mandate_india: IE3 (Premium Efficiency) minimum for motors 0.75kW-1000kW sold for new applications, mandatory since July 2023

efficiency_by_class_pct.IE4_super_premium: ~1-2 percentage points above IE3 (~90-95% range cited for IE3, >95% for IE4 in Step 15)

upgrade_gain.size_dependency: Internal efficiency loss from heat/friction can be as high as 20% in small motors but only 4-5% in motors above 160kW -- upgrade paybacks are much stronger for smaller motors.
upgrade_gain.real_world_example: Textile mill upgrading 50x15kW motors IE1->IE3 saved ~273,600 kWh/year

motor.real_lever_for_msmes: IE3->IE4 (since IE3 is now the mandated purchase floor, not an upgrade)

lifetime_years_iea_residential_reference.note: Residential/building-scale figure -- not validated for industrial process-heat scale equipment.

reference_case.project: BEE Pali Textile Cluster DPR, stenter waste heat recovery

run_hours_context.modeling_note: High utilization (run-hours) improves ROI for heat-related retrofits -- encode as a payback modifier.

thermal_storage.role: Key enabling technology to pair variable renewable electricity with continuous industrial heat demand (IEA).

hydrogen.maturity_flag: High cost/parameter uncertainty -- see technology_costs.json for full detail.

lifetime_assumptions_project_defaults.source: project master document defaults; IEA figures (Step 8) used only as a residential-scale cross-check, not primary

gaps_and_flags: Furnace efficiency has no single benchmark -- must be modeled per-process, not as a flat percentage.

BEE's primary sector-by-sector normalized energy consumption benchmarks (e.g. GJ/tonne for cement, steel) were not directly accessed -- recommend visiting beeindia.gov.in's PAT Scheme and Standards & Labeling sections directly.
IEA lifetime figures (10-17 years) are residential/building-scale, not industrial -- project's own defaults (boiler=15yr, motor=12yr) should take priority.
No IEA or BEE data found broken out specifically at MSME scale (as opposed to large industrial) -- capex/efficiency per unit may differ due to lost economies of scale at small installation sizes.
